tone_statements.quote: Mashi (Naki) (ISO 639-3: mff, mffy1238;) language is a Yemne-Kimbi (Good et al 2011) speech variety spoken in Lower Fungom in Menchum Division in the North West Region of Cameroon. The word list is collected from two frmale speakers of Mashi residing in Yaounde. There is individual-based variation among the two speakers at level of the tones, prefix, lexical root, even concord nuances.

tone_statements.citation: Good, Jeff & Jesse Lovegren. 2017. Remarks on the nasal classes in Mungbam and Naki. In R. Kramer & R. Kiessling (eds.), Mechthildian approaches to Afrikanistik. Koln: Koppe (preprint, 8 pp.).
tone_statements.quote: Noun class prefix tones in Naki can vary depending on the stem they attach to (Hombert 1980: 94), which is why they are not indicated with tones in the table. Gender 9/10 is coded purely via tone on the noun stem, where the singular form has a lower tone and the plural a higher tone, with the precise details depending on the stem itself (Hombert 1980: 91).
tone_statements.locator: preprint p. 8, sec. 3 'The nasal classes of Naki' (text under Table 11); also p. 4 (Munken concord tone diacritics) and p. 8 'Naki shows tone patterns in its noun class system similar to those seen in Western Grassfields'
tone_statements.summary: Naki (naki1238): lexical tone plus grammatical tone in the noun-class system - gender 9/10 singular vs plural marked solely by lower vs higher stem tone; prefix tone conditioned by the stem.

tone_statements.quote: There is clear evidence for the presence of four tone levels in Naki, as exemplified by the set of words gí ‘ egg’, lī ‘ tongue’, shè ‘ fowl’, and mȕ ‘ person’. The treatment of mȕ as super low as opposed to gí as super high reflects an impression regarding relative frequency, though this is not yet well substantiated. Contour tones are also frequently encountered, and some examples include ŋku᷅ŋ ‘ chief’, nya᷆m ‘ animals’, and bâm ‘ 2. my’. As suggested by these examples, the inventory of falling tones appears to be larger than that of rising tones.

tone_statements.quote: Tone should be reasonably accurate in surface terms. Some levels may be mistranscribed since a four-level distinction was only recently unambiguously uncovered, but places where a formal distinction is purely tonal should accurately reflect which class has a lower/higher tone than the other.
